Trump Accounts are new, tax-deferred, custodial investment accounts for children under 18 with Social Security numbers, launched via the "One Big Beautiful Bill" Act. They allow up to $5,000 in annual, post-tax contributions (starting July 2026) and feature a $1,000 federal pilot contribution for children born between 2025 and 2028. Key Details for Trump Accounts: Eligibility: U.S. citizen children under 18 at year-end. $1,000 Seed Money: Children born Jan. 1, 2025, to Dec. 31, 2028, receive a $1,000 contribution from the federal government. Contribution Limits: Up to $5,000 annually (post-tax) can be added, including contributions from employers, families, or organizations. Account Structure: Managed by adults as a custodial account until the child turns 18. Usage: Earnings grow tax-deferred for future expenses like college, home buying, or business startups. Opening the Account: Parents use IRS Form 4547 IRS Form 4547 specialized portal Important Information: The $1,000 contribution does not count toward the $5,000 annual limit. Funds are invested in index funds, with projected high growth over 18 years. This initiative was established to provide long-term savings opportunities and early financial empowerment. For more information, see the official Trump Accounts page on IRS.gov Trump Accounts page on IRS.gov
